label: Main listening room, 3D3A Lab, Princeton University
note: irregular, near-shoebox (paper Fig. 2b): 4.0 m wide, 7.6 m long, 2.5 m high, one long wall angled outward in two segments (6.1 and 5.5 m); no volume is stated (the 4.0 x 7.6 x 2.5 m rectangle is 76 m3); carpeted floor, walls and ceiling partly covered with acoustic panels; RT60 0.24 s (average over 1300-6300 Hz, Methods.txt); a linear array of 8 Focal Shape 40 woofers, not equalised (sources e0-e7, x -0.877 to 0.886 m), 0.85 m above the floor; B&K 4100 HATS with BACCH-BM Pro in-ear microphones on a translation platform and turntable; receiver = the file's y (Y_50cm to Y_100cm) and m, with x = -0.5 + 0.05 x (m // 37) m and head azimuth 180 + 5 x (m mod 37) degrees (270 faces the array, 180 faces left, 360 faces right); the files' z axis points down (ListenerUp), so the array centre (z 0.255 m) is below the ears; time zero is about 1 ms after emission (the direct sound arrives about 50 samples earlier than the distance gives; Data.Delay states 20 samples); 16384 samples (341 ms), high-passed at 100 Hz, globally normalised; Below 1 kHz the noise floor lies only 29-36 dB under the peak (125-500 Hz; 47-48 dB at 1-4 kHz), so two thirds of the IRs have no mid-band decay time and 99.5 % are graded C, most of all in Y_90cm to Y_100cm; where measured, rt_mid (0.25 s) and T30 at 1-4 kHz (0.26, 0.24, 0.23 s) agree with the authors' RT60 of 0.24 s (1.3-6.3 kHz)
